transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having these evenings after work where, especially if I’ve been really strict with food all day, I end up eating much more than I planned. It’ll start with dinner, and then cereal, crackers, leftovers, sweets—just a lot within a couple of hours.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, I keep finding myself going back to the kitchen, even though I’m telling myself to stop. I don’t really feel in control again until I’m uncomfortably full.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I’m not sure what you mean by “make myself”—I haven’t really thought about it that way.
After you overeat, do you ever intentionally vomit to try to get rid of the food?
I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t thought about it as intentionally trying to get rid of the food.
After these eating episodes, have you ever made yourself throw up?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
After these eating episodes, do you ever use laxatives to try to get rid of the food?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself using anything like that after eating.
After you eat this way, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself making myself vomit after eating.
After these eating episodes, do you ever fast the next day to make up for what you ate?
Yeah. The next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, telling myself I’m making up for it. Or I’ll take an extra-long hike or push myself harder at softball conditioning, even if I’m tired.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself throw up?
I don’t think I do. I haven’t noticed myself making myself throw up after those times.
Do you regularly do something after these eating episodes to prevent weight gain?
Yeah. The next day I usually try to make up for it by skipping breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a really long hike or push myself harder at softball conditioning, even if I’m already tired.
Have these eating episodes with trying to make up for them been happening at least once a week for the past 3 months?
Yeah… for the past few months, it’s been most weeks. Usually one or two nights where I eat a lot more than I meant to, and then the next day I skip meals or exercise longer to try to make up for it.
